resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO) on change of ownership
resale_co.issued_by: Construction Office (Construction Official, with the subcode officials)
resale_co.lead_time: Not stated. The Construction Office keeps office hours Tuesday and Thursday, 4:00 to 6:00 pm.
resale_co.valid_for: Not stated. A temporary certificate of continued occupancy, if granted, is valid for 180 days.
requirements: General inspection of the visible parts of the building; no pending violations or orders of the Construction Official
The current use of the building must have lawfully existed (checked against municipal records)
No violations of N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.14 and no unsafe conditions under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.32(a)

No City CCO application form is posted online; contact the Construction Office (143 Main Street; 609-652-8759; construction@portrepublicnj.org), open Tuesday and Thursday 4:00 to 6:00 pm, to request the inspection.

resale_co.notes: City Code Chapter 102 (Construction Codes, Uniform), read in full on ecode360, says a certificate of continued occupancy is required for the occupancy of any existing building upon a change of ownership or a new tenant (§102-9). The fee is unclear: the fee schedule in §102-4 (amended 12-8-2015) lists 'Certificate of continued occupancy: $100 per unit', while the older §102-9 text (1989) still says $25. The newer $100 figure is probably current, but confirm. The Construction Office web page does not mention a resale CCO or post an application, so confidence is medium until the office confirms it still performs these inspections on sales. If improvements are needed, the Construction Official may grant a temporary CCO valid 180 days, with a $50 per day penalty after that period (§102-10). The Rental Registration Application (Inspection Fee $100.00, Re-Inspection Fee $35.00) is for rentals only and is not a resale requirement.

requirements: Smoke alarms on each level and outside each separate sleeping area, per N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19 (battery-only alarms must be 10-year sealed units)
Carbon monoxide alarm in the immediate vicinity of the sleeping areas (homes with a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage)
The 2025 state law (P.L.2025, c.19) removed the portable fire extinguisher from the state sale certificate

fire_cert.notes: NJ DCA lists Port Republic as State enforced (S) in its July 2026 LEA registry, and its July 17, 2026 list marks Port Republic 'SC' (the State issues smoke certificates). The state fire directory lists 'NJ Division Fire Safety' for smoke detector compliance in Port Republic. State fees ($45 / $90 / $161 by business days before the change of occupant) are cited from the N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9(d) adoption in the NJ Register. The City's Construction Office page lists Pat Naticchione as Fire Inspector & Fire Subcode, but that is a construction code role; no City page mentions issuing resale smoke certificates. The directory gives (609) 633-6132 for Louis Kilmer; the Bureau's own page gives (609) 633-6106, which is used here.
